page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors built on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at 2.8 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32 GB of system memory. This yields an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The r8gd family integrates 237 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Accelerated graphics hardware is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution across general compute and memory workflows. In compute benchmarks, the instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1864.0 and a multi-core score of 5890.0, alongside stress-ng results of 1707.39 single-core and 6817.45 multi-core. Cryptographic and vector-heavy tests reflect ARMv9 instruction handling, showing AES support but registering weaker scores on legacy x86-oriented PassMark suites, such as a 3927.91 overall CPU score. Memory performance shows solid bandwidth characteristics, maintaining 96.75 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 44.6 GB/sec on writes, which aids data retrieval tasks.

Workload evaluation highlights strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.27 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Key-value operations using Redis reach 8.45 million operations per second, complemented by PassMark database operation results of 5938.4. In contrast, large language model inference is constrained by core count and lack of accelerators, reaching only 6.18 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage combined with a generous memory allocation provides high density for caching layers, in-memory key-value databases, real-time analytics, and data transformation jobs that require temporary scratch space without incurring extra network storage latency.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Equipped with 32 GB of memory, the instance delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 237 GB of integrated NVMe SSD instance storage and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate solid memory bandwidth with uncached reads reaching 96.75 GB/sec and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.27 GB/sec. General multi-core throughput delivers consistent median performance, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5890.0 and Redis throughput reaching 8.45 million operations per second. However, compute-heavy LLM inference remains limited due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. The configuration delivers efficient memory density and fast local scratch space, making it appropriate for in-memory databases, Redis caching tiers, real-time analytics, and distributed processing workloads.
